clue.text: Tiny piece about centrally stripped grammatical form

indicators.note: about means going round, so the tiny piece wraps the other letters

parts.note: a particle is a minute piece of matter

indicators.note: centrally points to the two middle letters of the word stripped

parts.note: its central pair of letters is used

explanation.surface: A tiny bit of something seems to be described as stripped in the middle, then oddly called a grammatical form.
explanation.definitionFit: A participle is a verb form such as 'running' or 'stolen', a standard term of grammar.

clue.text: Confuse order to let one's hair down?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to baffle or confuse

definitions.text: order to let one's hair down?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: '...!', a command to relax and behave less inhibitedly

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BE WILDER and it becomes an instruction to loosen up; the question mark flags the playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder someone is to perplex them so they cannot think clearly, a plain synonym of confusing them.

clue.text: Mostly wonderful, tense batter's innings

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: wicked is slang for wonderful or excellent
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone praises a batter's innings as wonderful but tense.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batter's stay at the crease is counted in wickets, so a wicket can stand for the partnership or innings that ends when one falls.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket terminology a wicket can denote the period a batsman stays in, i.e. the stint before dismissal.

clue.text: Engineer, eh? So it's said

indicators.note: so it's said tells us to go by how the word is spoken out loud

parts.note: 'eh?' is a way of saying 'what?' when you mishear

explanation.surface: Someone queries an engineer with a puzzled 'eh?', as if repeating what they heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eh?' means 'What?', which in many British accents is said just like the name of James Watt.
explanation.definitionFit: James Watt was the Scottish engineer whose improvements to the steam engine powered the Industrial Revolution.

clue.text: Character in Othello reported noble group of stars

parts.note: Cassio is Othello's lieutenant in Shakespeare's play

indicators.note: reported means the word for noble is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a peer is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A character in Othello is said to have been reported to a noble astronomical group.
explanation.walkthrough: PEER said aloud, in a non-rhotic British accent, matches the ending PEIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassiopeia is a W-shaped constellation of the northern sky, named after a queen of Greek myth.

clue.text: Damn shower beginning to irritate Gulf national

parts.note: 'bah!' is an exclamation of annoyance, like 'damn!'
a shower is a short spell of rain

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone curses a downpour that begins to irritate a person from the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bahraini is a citizen of Bahrain, an island kingdom in the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Covering of slate on a dam

parts.note: to slate a play is to pan it, i.e. criticise harshly
a dam is a mother, especially of an animal, so MA

explanation.surface: It describes the covering laid of slate on top of a dam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam' seems to be a reservoir wall, but it is the old word for a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A panama is a lightweight straw hat, a covering for the head.

clue.text: Extremely fickle twin sons own up

indicators.note: extremely points to the outermost letters, first and last, of the word fickle

parts.note: its two end letters are used
S is the abbreviation for son, so two of them make SS

explanation.surface: Fickle twin boys are told to own up to something.
explanation.definitionFit: To fess up is an informal phrase for confessing, so the word means admit or confess.

clue.text: Mike and Heather enthralled by an advanced style of country music?

indicators.note: enthralled by means held inside, so the letters go within the word an

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
erica is the botanical name for heather
A is a common abbreviation for advanced, as in A-level

explanation.surface: Two people, Mike and Heather, are captivated by an advanced form of country music.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike and Heather look like a couple, but they are M and ERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana is a roots genre blending folk, country and blues; the question mark hints it also means things typical of America.

clue.text: Fast vehicle ditched by Shell?

indicators.note: ditched by means the vehicle is thrown out of the shell word

parts.note: a carapace is the hard upper shell of a crab or tortoise
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A speedy vehicle is abandoned by the oil company Shell.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Shell' suggests the oil company, but it is a plain shell, a carapace.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an adverb meaning quickly or at speed, as in 'work continued apace'.

clue.text: Knitter knitted knick-knack

indicators.note: knitted means the letters are worked together into a new pattern, as yarn is

explanation.surface: A knitter has knitted a little ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinket is a small ornament or piece of jewellery of little value, so a synonym for a knick-knack.

clue.text: Excel is almost certain to change

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: sure means certain
to pass can mean to change from one state to another, as water passes into ice

explanation.surface: Someone predicts the Excel spreadsheet program is almost certain to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excel' looks like the software, but it is the verb, to do better than.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass is to outdo or go beyond, the same as to excel over something.

clue.text: Force trainee to execute 'duck and cover', primarily when retreating

indicators.note: when retreating means the string of letters is read backwards
primarily points to the first letter of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A recruit in the forces is trained to perform the duck-and-cover drill while falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of 'to execute duck and cover' are TEDAC; 'when retreating' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person training to become an officer in the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Old New Zealand admiral on manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres means moving about, so the letters of admiral on are deployed in a new order

explanation.surface: An old New Zealand admiral is out on naval exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: Maoriland was a nineteenth-century literary name for New Zealand, after its Maori people.

clue.text: Spell in which nobody gets the runs

definitions.text: Spell in which nobody gets the runs

parts.words: Spell in which nobody gets the runs
parts.note: a cricket over of six balls from which the batters score no runs; the surface suggests a bout free of diarrhoea

explanation.walkthrough: 'The runs' is slang for diarrhoea, so it reads as a healthy spell; in cricket an over is a bowler's spell of six balls, and one with no runs scored is a maiden.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a maiden over is a set of six deliveries in which the batting side scores nothing.

clue.text: Style doctor introducing several points

parts.note: eight compass points in a row: E, S, S, S, E, N, S, E

explanation.surface: A stylish doctor is introducing a few points about fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'points' are compass points, East, South, North and so on, strung together to spell ESSSENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress sense is a flair for choosing clothes that look good, i.e. sartorial taste.

clue.text: Literary adventurer disturbed lingerer grabbing tool for opening letter

indicators.note: for opening means the letter's spelt-out name is prised open so the rest can go inside it

parts.note: the letter P is spelt out as PEE

indicators.note: grabbing means the rearranged letters take hold of the tool, which sits inside them
disturbed means the letters of lingerer are thrown into disorder and rearranged

parts.note: a pick is a digging tool

explanation.surface: A literary adventurer is disturbed by someone lingering with a tool for opening a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tool for opening letter' reads as a letter-opener, but the tool is just PICK, and 'for opening' tells you to open up PEE, the spelt-out letter P, and put everything else in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Peregrine Pickle is the roguish hero of Tobias Smollett's 1751 picaresque novel of that name.

clue.text: Alcohol clergy bottled at home

indicators.note: bottled is slang for drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: The clergy keep alcohol bottled up at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottled' seems to mean stored in bottles, but here it means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Glycerin, or glycerol, is chemically a trihydric alcohol, a sweet syrupy compound.

clue.text: Lock web address after X linked to copyright

indicators.note: after means the web address is placed following the other pieces
linked to means the kiss is joined directly to the copyright sign

parts.note: an X at the end of a letter stands for a kiss
C is the abbreviation for copyright, as in the circled C symbol
a URL is the address of a web page

explanation.surface: A web address is posted on X, the social network, with a copyright notice attached.
explanation.walkthrough: X looks like the social media site, but it is the kiss at the end of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss-curl is a small curl of hair pressed flat on the forehead or cheek, a lock of hair.

clue.text: Condition may seem poor around edges of pitch

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the others
poor means the letters are in bad shape and must be reworked
edges of points to the first and last letters of the word pitch

parts.note: its two end letters are used

explanation.surface: A sports pitch may look in poor condition around its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: MAY SEEM rearranged gives EMYSEMA, which goes around PH.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphysema is a lung disease in which the air sacs are damaged, a chronic medical condition.

clue.text: Beggar's right to stop one who'll cough up

definitions.note: read as 'Beggar is': a prayer is one who prays or begs

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the letter goes into the middle

parts.note: to cough up is to pay, so the one who pays is a payer

explanation.surface: A beggar asserts a right to stop someone and make them hand over money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beggar's' is 'Beggar is'; a prayer here is one who prays, i.e. begs earnestly.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer, pronounced to rhyme with player, is a person who entreats or supplicates, much as a beggar does.

clue.text: Nine divine females married pursuers off and on

indicators.note: off and on means letters are skipped and taken in turn, picking alternate ones

parts.note: its second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters are used

explanation.surface: Nine goddesses, wed, have had suitors chasing them intermittently.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muses were the nine goddesses of Greek myth who inspired the arts and sciences.

clue.text: Tiny setter's amphibian is caught

indicators.note: caught means heard, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: the setter's means 'my', the setter speaking of themselves; a newt is a small amphibian

explanation.surface: The setter's tiny amphibian has been captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My newt' said aloud matches the adjective meaning tiny, pronounced my-NEWT.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute, stressed on the second syllable, is an adjective meaning extremely small.

clue.text: Notice call to work

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to give someone the ... is to dismiss them, i.e. give notice
second meaning: '...!' is a sailors' cry used when hauling together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb meaning spot, but it is the notice of dismissal from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a rhythmic shout to coordinate pulling on ropes and a slang term for being sacked.

clue.text: Catch punch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... is a fastener or catch, or to ... a fish is to catch it
second meaning: a short swinging blow in boxing

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a curved fastening or angling device and a boxer's bent-arm blow.

clue.text: Handcuff a salt arrested by setter

indicators.note: arrested by means held inside, so the letters go within the setter's word

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as ME
NaCl is the chemical formula for common salt, sodium chloride

explanation.surface: A sailor is arrested by the setter and handcuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A salt' looks like a sailor, but salt is the chemical NaCl.
explanation.definitionFit: A manacle is a metal band or chain used to fetter the wrists, a synonym for handcuff.

clue.text: Bible book briefly picked up before end of religious service

indicators.note: picked up means lifted, so in this down entry the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: Sam is the short form of Samuel, a book of the Old Testament

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: its last letter is used

explanation.surface: A Bible is briefly picked up before the close of a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass is the Eucharistic service of the Catholic Church, a religious service.

clue.text: Wrestler returned inside box-like zone

indicators.note: returned means the letters found are read backwards
inside means the letters sit within the words box-like zone

explanation.surface: A wrestler goes back into a ring-like square zone.
explanation.definitionFit: An ozeki is a champion rank in sumo, just below yokozuna, so a sumo wrestler.

clue.text: Mobile meters, say — one way to repay debt

indicators.note: mobile means moving, so these letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Portable meters are suggested as one way to pay off a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy terms are a credit arrangement letting a buyer pay by small instalments over time.
